explanation: Maintain the smallest possible final value for each subsequence length. Binary search for the first tail strictly greater than the new value, allowing equal values to extend a nondecreasing subsequence.
attribution: Original C# implementation written for EPI Practice from the displayed contract; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: For every stored length, tails holds the smallest ending value attainable for a subsequence of that length. Replacing the first tail strictly greater than a new value preserves those possibilities while making future extensions no harder. Appending when no such tail exists proves a longer subsequence is attainable; allowing equal tails makes the subsequence nondecreasing.
walkthrough: For [3,1,1,2], tails changes [3]→[1]→[1,1]→[1,1,2]. The equal 1 extends rather than replaces the first slot, so the answer is 3.
edgeCases: Equal values may all belong to the subsequence.
